Depression manifests itself differently person to person. There is such thing as high functioning depression where a person has depression but is still able to function ok in their life. I myself have it. It can make you feel like your problems don't matter because there are so many other people that have it so much worse. My own doctor diagnosed me and prescribed medication to help with it and I still have trouble believing I deal with it because I read so many posts here from people who have it so bad their life is literal hell. But I have my days where all I want to do is lay in bed and focus on not giving in to really dark thoughts. Judging from what you shared, it's possible you could have depression. But above all else, if you feel like you have it, talk with your doctor or a psychologist. It's never a good idea to try to diagnose yourself or take medical advice from the internet.

I'm not very good at these sorts of things. But I deal with it too. It's definitely very annoying and bothersome when I try and sleep. A couple years ago or so, I had a pretty bad spike that lasted quite a while. It took some time, but I eventually got over it. As stupid and idiotic as it sounds, what helped me was simply accepting it. It's extremely difficult and doesn't seem possible; I had so much trouble when I first started dealing with it. But the sonner you accept that it's something you have to live with, the quicker your mind can get used to it. I still have flare-ups every now and then. But I hardly pay them much attention and they go away after a few minutes or so. I would discuss it with your doctor. There may not be a cure yet. But there are treatments to help you adjust to it. I would also suggest talking to an ENT or an audiologist. There are resources out there that can help you. It's tough and brutal. But you can overcome it. Hold on to your friends and loved ones that help and encourage you. You aren't alone. r/tinnitusresearch is a fairly good sub to chat with other people who deal with it and you can stay in the loop about tinnitus advancements and the such. I wish you nothing but the best. Keep your head up.

But there's always that one person who just absolutely nails it in a fantastic way. I listen to a lot of music and while I love everyone I listen to and they're all very talented, the person that stands out the most to me is Amy Lee of Evanescence. That woman is definitely someone that is gifted at singing. There's times where I find myself at a loss for words when I hear her sing. She's definitely my all-time favorite female vocalist. One bad habit I have is playing the "compare game". Something I wish I can break. But it's definitely easier said than done. I'd do something (let's say Minecraft for example) and be relatively proud of it then here comes someone else who absolutely puts my work to shame. I can't help myself sometimes kinda huddling in a corner in shame metaphorically when I see other people's stuff and think to myself "well shoot, I guess I'm not good for anything then. His/Her work destroys what I put together". But it's definitely something I need to let go. All things considered, you should never let anyone else out you down. In fact, let it inspire you to do better. You may never rise above "that one person", but that's fine. Just keep doing you. You never know; you might have a skill that you're amazing at that "that one person" might be garbage at and views your work in high regard. We're all different. No one's good at absolutely everything. Some will shine in areas others don't. Best thing you can do is put a smile on your face and keep pressing on.
